description:

Shulin Ling was one of seven arrested on April 30th, a tragic protest that's compared to Tiananman Square.

The case with the grand jury is scheduled on this day. Several city council members have written letters in support of Shu Ling. After reviewing the evidence, the case ruled her as not guilty.

Then again, we don't hope that so we can win.

Result: the prosecutor from the DA's office officially prosecuted her on 08:40 AM, just an hour before the court case. Not only is this an outrage of justice, but a disrespect to the court's time & entire legal process.

title: Adjourned Court Case
description: Westhab aka Coyle Properties LLC lost the court case on May 7th to access the homeowner's backyard and they filed another case to gain access. Supporters & homeowners took a tour bus to the courtroom, showing our large numbers. As if losing the first case on May 7th wasn't humiliating enough, Westhab's lawyer showed up in a wheelchair. His legs weren't the only thing that's disabled, as they did not prepare the proper documents to show their case. The next court appearance will be Sept 24th.

title: Court Case of Jenny Ma
description:
Location: 120 Schermerhorn St, AP-3

Jenny Ma was one of seven arrested on the April 30th, a tragic protest that's compared to Tiananman Square. We hope that the charges against her are dropped, just like the five others who were arrested at the same protest.

title: Press Conference at Base
description: CBS came to the base to interview several politicians: Lester Chang, Steve Chan, Mercedes, Susan Zhuang, and Mike Novakov.

title: National Night Out at 61st Precint
description:
Location: 61st Precint

National Night Out is an annual community-building campaign that promotes police-community partnerships and neighborhood relationships. It takes place on the first Tuesday of August in most areas and events often include block parties, cookouts, and opportunities to meet local officers and learn about crime prevention.

title: Curtis Sliwa visits the Base Camp
description:
Location: Coyle Street

Red Hat Curtis and his wife Nancy pays a visit to the base camp and sits down and chats with the protestors. After that, Red Hat Curtis and his wife went to Coney Island.

title: Anti-Adams Protest
description: This protest took place on 8th ave & 65th street. A group of communists support Mayor Adams as he made a speech. A second larger group, led by your leaders Ronbo, Andy, and Benjamin Louie, protested against Adams and his misguided supporters. Police were present at the scene but it ended entirely peaceful. Lester Chang and Steve Chan were present to speak to the news. YT Video Citizen Weixin

title: Curtis's Campaign Speech
description: Red Hat Curtis decided to hold a campaign speech at the base camp, speaking to how poorly Eric Adams has managed the city. Mamdami is a communist and should never hold office, and Communist Cuomo killed hundreds of nursing home seniors. Other speakers include your leaders Ronbo, Andy, and Benjamin Louie, as well as two cute little ones. Video

title: 86st's Victory & 1 Year Anniversary
description: It is the one year anniversary of the 86st protests against the homeless shelter. On this day, the leaders of 86st street celebrated their victory. Many politicians, including Susan Zhuang, Steven Chan and Lester Chang made speeches and there was food and drinks. Video

title: Electrified Election Day
description: Many volunteers helped Dimple Willabus out, sat at tables and passed out flyers in 100 degree weather. At 9pm, Dimple had a celebratory dinner with her team and made a speech.

title: Kings Plaza Rally
description: Two rallies—one starting on Coyle Street and the other on Flatbush Avenue—came together as a single protest at Kings Plaza. The MC was Ronnie 'Ronbo' the community champion and the speakers were Senator Stephan Chan, Assemblyman Lester Chang, Lina Chen, Dimple Willabus, and the people's mayor, Curtis Sliwa. They spoke against the shelters and lithium ion batteries, both toxic elements to the community. Citizens Youtube

title: Motherfucker's Day Celebration
description: The group of protestors and neighbors celebrated Mothers Day with a lot of food. It was a huge community event, people brought their parents and kids.

title: Charges dropped for arrested
description: On April 30th, seven were arrested during the protests that lasted all day. All arrestees had their court cases on this day and 5 out of 7 had their charges dropped while two others had their cases delayed. This proves that most of the charges were bogus.

title: City Hall Protest
description: Energized by their court victory, the protestors' morale was sky high and they marched to City Hall to continue protesting the homeless shelter. Citizens

title: Court Date vs Westhab Part 2
description: As homeowners went to court to fight Westhab's access to their backyard, hundreds of protesters stood outside to protest against Westhab's corporate ambitions and support the working class homeowners. Result: the court ruled that Westhab's claims were bogus as it was a bait and switch, and denied them access to the backyard. Citizens Court Docs

title: Save South Brooklyn
description: Hundreds of protesters marched down Avenue U, starting from Coyle Street. Cars honked as they drove by, showing their support for our cause. This massive protest was led by red hat Curtis Sliwa and Steve Chan, and managed by Lina and Dimple Willabus. The rally ended at Coney Island Avenue, where Curtis made a speech. It was the first time in history Ave U has seen such a huge rally. News Youtube 1 Youtube 2

title: Tragedy on Coyle Street
description:
Hundreds of protesters clashed with police officers that lasted from morning till night. Seven were arrested and a few others were sent to the hospital. Several videos popped up online showing police brutality, ganging up on the elderly and women. CBS PIX11 LLN
Clip 1 Clip 2 Clip 3 Curtis

title: Base Camp was expanded
description: On this day, more tents were added to the base camp to expand to the size matching the lot. With so many chairs, tables and tents to protect them from the rain, more people were able to show up and hang out.

title: Dimple Visits the Base
description: Though Dimple does not live near the shelter, she comes out frequently to check up on the people and offer encouragement. One can make the argument she is doing this because she's running for office, but how many candidates visit as frequently as she does?

title: Court Date Part 1
description: Coyle Street LLC, aka Westhab hired three lawyers to sue our homeowners to gain access to the backyard. Behind the lot of 2134 Coyle are five homes sharing one driveway which lead to the lot's behind. Led by a mysterious leader, A group of volunteers protested outside the courtroom, getting attention of local news. Link Court Docs

title: Protest Against Mercedes's Office
description: Residents of District 46 who were unhappy with Mercedes's inaction regarding the shelter organized a protest in front of her office. Mercedes retaliated by taking Dimple to court, trying to knock her off the ballot.

title: First Night Shift
description: Right after the intense meeting at the community board, at around 6am the next morning, a construction truck appeared at the lot. At the time, no permits existed for any kind of work, so protestors appeared to block the employees from entering the building. Later that night, some neighbors decided to do a night shift to watch out for future sneaky attacks. This group of eight warriors lasted until the morning, when the morning shift came out to take over.

title: Community Chaos at Kingsborough
description: Westhab presented its plans for the 'Coyle Street Family Center' to a packed room of Sheepshead Bay residents. The meeting became heated as residents voiced strong opposition, feeling they were misled about the project's nature. Link 1 Link 2 Link 3 Link 4

title: Bait & Switch
description: Residents and local leaders expressed opposition to the proposed shelter, citing concerns about safety. Among the attendees was Curtis Sliwa, candidate for mayor, who called this a bait and switch and encouraged citizens to protest for the safety of their homes. Around this time, an online petition appeared to oppose the shelter. Link

title: Initial Protests
description: Hundreds of community members and local politicians, protested the city's decision to replace the planned affordable housing with a homeless shelter. The biggest supporters are Dimple Willabus, candidate for City Council D46, as well as Curtis Sliwa, candidate for Mayor. Source

title: 86st First Protest
description: It was one year ago when Mayor Adams sent the police to remove protestors from the homeless shelter to allow the construction conmen to do their work. Many of them were arrested and Susan Zhuang bit the captain on the arm to protect a senior from being trapped.
